content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on a link, which is exactly what the rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings", "rule_words": "A judge may not rest STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED on one verse failing to state a link or its contrary.", "room": "'rest ... on one verse failing to state a link or its contrary': (1) resting the UNDERDETERMINED verdict on the single verse's admitted ambiguity is the forbidden rest; (2) merely citing where each side answered does not add independent footing, so the verdict rests on Matthew 1:16 alone.", "why": "The judge rests the UNDERDETERMINED verdict solely on Matthew 1:16 admitting both readings, which is precisely the one-verse rest the rule forbids."}
